RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

The panel's composition is not evidence of anything on its own. All-female panels occur routinely in many departments, and leading with it will read as insinuation rather than argument — it tends to discredit otherwise legitimate complaints.

Your stronger ground is substantive and procedural: a candidate with a completed PhD, six papers and four years' teaching lost to someone still finishing a doctorate with two papers, and you've had no written reasons after two weeks. Public universities usually owe you those reasons, and often an appeal window that is already running.

So: send a firm written follow-up citing the relevant rules, ask for panel scoring against the advertised criteria, and judge the decision on what comes back. Industry experience can legitimately be weighted heavily — but it should be visible in the criteria.
